question: Under what striking condition is even a wise person said to be burning, according to this clause?
premises: Reference is made to the tip of nectar and to the tip of juice as instruments.
A wise person is described as burning.
The particle 'also' marks a contrast despite wisdom.
inference: Even a wise person, while in the condition described, is burning at the tip of nectar or by means of the tip of juice.
uncertainties: The exact technical procedure referred to is not fully specified by this verse alone.
plain_english: Even a wise person, burning, [acts] at the tip of nectar with the tip of juice.
